sentences.quote: Florent Menegaux, born in 1962, has been president of the Michelin Group since May 2019, when he succeeded Jean-Dominique Senard after Senard moved to Renault.
sentences.text: Florent Menegaux, born in 1962, has led Michelin as president of the group since May 2019, taking over from Jean-Dominique Senard when the latter moved to Renault.

sentences.quote: After graduating in finance and economics from Paris-Dauphine University, Menegaux joined PricewaterhouseCoopers in 1986 as a consultant specializing in interest rate risk management for banks. He then spent time in logistics at Exel Logistics and Norbert Dentressangle before joining Michelin in 1997 as commercial director for truck tires in the UK and Ireland.
sentences.text: A graduate in finance and economics from Paris-Dauphine University, he began his career at PricewaterhouseCoopers in 1986 advising banks on interest rate risk management, then worked in logistics at Exel Logistics and Norbert Dentressangle before joining Michelin in 1997 as commercial director for truck tires in the UK and Ireland.

He subsequently held roles across nearly every geography and product line, including North America, South America, Africa/Middle East and Europe, becoming chief operating officer in 2014 and CEO in 2019.
Investors generally view this trajectory favorably: he is a Michelin lifer and an operational executive rather than a financial engineer.

mgmt_recent.text: In January 2026 SAGES renewed Florent Menegaux's term as Managing General Partner for up to four years, unanimously approved by the Supervisory Board chaired by Barbara Dalibard, while Yves Chapot chose not to seek renewal and Philippe Jacquin was proposed as General Manager, voted at the May 22, 2026 Shareholders Meeting. Benedicte de Bonnechose, an Executive Committee member since 2021 overseeing Europe and the transportation business lines, became Chief Financial Officer on June 1, 2026, succeeding Chapot. On French plant closures, Menegaux cited low-cost Asian tire competition, European overcapacity and falling volumes.
